topic: pg_clickhouse v0.10 Guide 2026: Subquery Pushdown and 1000x Faster TPC-H Queries

key_points: Official v0.10.0 release post (Aug 11, 2026) by Josh Ventura; headline feature is SubPlan (subquery) pushdown via PR #289
TPC-H scoreboard moved from 12 to 16 of 22 queries fully pushed down; only 6 remain (Q13, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q20, Q21)
Q17 is the trophy: correlated subquery averaging l_quantity per part went from 32.7s (v0.3, local eval per row) to 37ms fully pushed down — ~880x, beating native PostgreSQL's 2.1s
Q2: 3,446ms (v0.3) → 24ms (v0.10); Q22: 1,415ms → 45ms (pushed as multiple foreign scans, ✼)
Subqueries in Postgres become subqueries in ClickHouse; EXPLAIN shows the whole comparison incl. subquery in one Remote SQL statement
NOT IN pushed via LEFT ANTI JOIN when planner can prove the transformation safe
Requires ClickHouse 25.8+ for correlated-subquery SQL shape; older servers fall back to local evaluation
IN/NULL semantics rabbit hole: ClickHouse uses two-valued logic, Postgres three-valued; v0.10 adds compensating CASE guards, tracks how each expression result is consumed
transform_null_in 0 added to default pg_clickhouse.session_settings so server profiles can't silently change IN semantics

Broadened pushdown: statistical aggregates (corr, covar_pop/samp, stddev, var, any_value), ordered-set aggregates (percentile_cont/disc → quantiles/quantileExactLow), partitionwise aggregation, encode(bytea,...), 3-arg ltrim/rtrim/btrim, interval arithmetic on date/timestamp
Driver: rebuilt on ClickHouse/clickhouse-c C client (v0.3.1), HTTP driver now uses Native format, fetch_size deprecated, 64MiB insert flush, per-scan connections fix concurrency crashes
New surface: clickhouse_query(server, sql), clickhouse_perform(server, sql) procedure, clickhouse_server_version(server); clickhouse_raw_query() deprecated
Builtin function pushdown is now opt-in (since v0.3.0) to preserve Postgres semantics (e.g. trig functions raise vs NaN)
Original December launch post; pg_clickhouse runs analytics queries on ClickHouse from PostgreSQL without rewriting SQL
Supports PostgreSQL 13+ and ClickHouse v23+

December headline: teaching planner to push a whole correlated EXISTS subquery down as a single LEFT SEMI JOIN instead of a nested loop with one ClickHouse round trip per outer row — moved from 3 to 12 of 22 TPC-H queries

Roadmap included: remaining 10 TPC-H queries, ClickBench pushdown, all aggregates/functions, comprehensive subquery pushdown, server/user-level settings, all CH data types, lightweight DELETE/UPDATE, batch COPY
At launch only 3 of 22 TPC-H queries fully pushed down
Authoritative source repo (269 stars); README contains full TPC-H benchmark table at scale factor 1 on MacBook Pro M4 Max 36GB
Docker quickstart: docker run ghcr.io/clickhouse/pg_clickhouse:18, then CREATE EXTENSION pg_clickhouse
README TPC-H table shows per-query Postgres vs pg_clickhouse timings and pushdown markers (✔ full single foreign scan, ✼ multiple foreign scans)
Docs: Reference (doc/pg_clickhouse.md) and Tutorial (doc/tutorial.md)
Reference doc: IN and NULL Semantics section documents two-valued vs three-valued logic handling
IN family (IN, NOT IN, = ANY, = ALL, <> ANY, <> ALL) pushes down unconditionally over constant list/array; guarded CASE form for nullable cases
NOT IN (SELECT ...) over nullable columns pushes down with compensating guards; NOT NULL declarations let cheaper unguarded form ship
IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA auto-declares non-Nullable ClickHouse columns as NOT NULL to maximize pushdown
transform_null_in = 1 breaks semantics of every pushed IN
Pushdown functions/operators/aggregates/ordered-set aggregates/window functions documented
Setup walkthrough: start ClickHouse via Docker (docker run -d --network host --name clickhouse -p 8123:8123 -p9000:9000 clickhouse)
Create tables, import NYC taxi dataset via s3() function, then query through pg_clickhouse
Shows how to import ClickHouse tables and push down queries from Postgres

stats.fact: pg_clickhouse v0.10.0 released Aug 11, 2026; TPC-H scoreboard moved from 12 to 16 of 22 queries fully pushed down
TPC-H Q17 (correlated subquery averaging l_quantity per part) went from 32.7s (v0.3, local eval per row) to 37ms fully pushed down — roughly 880x faster, beating native PostgreSQL's 2.1s
Subquery (SubPlan) pushdown requires ClickHouse 25.8 or later; older servers evaluate the subquery locally
pg_clickhouse supports PostgreSQL 13+ and ClickHouse v23+ (minimum ClickHouse 23.3)
At December launch only 3 of 22 TPC-H queries fully pushed down; December semi-join work moved it to 12
6 TPC-H queries remain unpushed: Q13, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q20, Q21 — blocked by join-tree-on-both-sides deparser limitation
ClickHouse evaluates IN under two-valued logic vs PostgreSQL three-valued; v0.10 adds compensating CASE guards and sets transform_null_in 0 by default
Binary driver rebuilt on ClickHouse/clickhouse-c C client; HTTP driver now uses Native format; fetch_size deprecated
New API: clickhouse_query(server, sql), CALL clickhouse_perform(server, sql), clickhouse_server_version(server); clickhouse_raw_query() deprecated

angles: The '1000x' story is real but nuanced: Q17 is ~880x (32.7s→37ms) and beats native Postgres; frame as 'orders of magnitude' rather than a blanket claim
Subquery pushdown is the missing piece that finally makes correlated subqueries (the queries that used to fetch every row individually) run entirely on ClickHouse
The IN/NULL semantics rabbit hole is a great 'why this is hard' angle — two-valued vs three-valued logic silently inverts results, and v0.10's guards are the fix
Practical how-to: verify pushdown with EXPLAIN (VERBOSE, COSTS OFF) and check the Remote SQL contains the subquery
Version gate: ClickHouse 25.8+ required for the new subquery pushdown — a key upgrade consideration
Declaring columns NOT NULL (or using IMPORT FOREIGN SCHEMA) maximizes pushdown by enabling cheaper unguarded forms
Architecture shift: opt-in builtin pushdown since v0.3.0 preserves Postgres semantics — trustworthy pushdown list
